svg.text: Landfills run out of room by filling up, not by speeding up
a planner modelling when a specific site closes
whether to model intake growth or just remaining
intake rate predicts closure better than fill level
share of permitted capacity already used
27 marks sit on an axis bound
The emergency is on the right edge, not the top: 59 of the 80 sites under five years are 90% full or more. That is a siting problem, not an intake problem.
The median landfill is 53% full and consumes 1.6% of itself a year, which is 62 years of design life at today's rate — most of the register is in no hurry.
863 open sites, the ones reporting all three numbers. Both causes are measured against permitted capacity, so a permit expansion moves a mark left and down at once.
